It defines the input form shapes (BookingForm, NoteForm), turns form fields into call arguments (for example, new Date(form.startsAt)), hands the work to the injected business services (SchedulingService, VisitNotesService), and formats the results with the presenter. It contains no persistence or transport code, and it makes no business decisions: no validation rules, no conflict checks, no state changes. One borderline spot is addNote, which returns how many notes exist (`notesFor(id).length`). That only shapes the response for display, so it is not a business rule. Passing the current time with new Date() in cancel just supplies a value from the request and leaves the cancellation rules to the service.
